div.p: Standard schedulers might place two pods on two different physical nodes because they are "LeastAllocated." In ML, this is a disaster for performance because communication between those pods must now travel over the relatively slow network.

li.p: The Goal: You want a scheduler that uses MostAllocated (Bin-Packing) to squeeze pods onto the same physical GPU node.
The Benefit: This allows pods to communicate over NVLink (which can be 10x–50x faster than standard Ethernet), drastically reducing training time.

div.div:
Standard Method: Use Pod Affinity and Node Selectors.
The "Workaround":
-affinity:
podAffinity:requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution
- label
Selector:matchLabels:
job: my-training-runtopology
Key: "kubernetes.io/hostname
The Result: This forces Pod 2 to go exactly where Pod 1 went.
The Failure Point: This only works if Pod 1 finds a home. If you have 100 pods, writing these rules for every single pod becomes a management nightmare. A custom scheduler does this automatically for the whole "batch."
